name: SMITH (Shared Memory Integrated Tool Hub)
venue: arXiv:2512.11303 (cs.CL, submitted 2025-12-12); also under OpenReview submission (id=JnwClln80Q). No peer-reviewed venue confirmed.
authors_affiliation: Jiarun Liu, Shiyue Xu, Yang Li, Shangkun Liu, Yongli Yu, Peng Cao (Caopeng). Affiliation: JD.com (author emails are @jd.com, e.g. liujiarun.1@jd.com).
code_url: N/A (no official code repository disclosed in the paper or found via search; the paper references manually-crafted tools and prompts only in appendices)
task_domain: tool-use / agent (dynamic tool creation) combined with general AI assistant task-solving requiring reasoning, multi-modality handling, web search, code execution, and tool-use, evaluated on the GAIA benchmark.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-task-at-inference but cross-task-accumulating setting. A multi-agent workflow (planner + developer-tester inner loop) solves GAIA tasks by iteratively writing/testing code in a Python sandbox (tool creation) and by retrieving prior successful execution experiences (experience sharing). It is training-free / cold-start (no parameter fine-tuning); memory grows online across tasks. The system addresses two coupled bottlenecks: limited predefined tool coverage and lack of systematic experience reuse. Multiple specialized sub-agents each keep their own episodic memory repository, so experience is shared across tasks and across the planner/developer roles (cross-agent within the workflow).
what_is_retrieved: experiences (episodic trajectories of past successful tasks), agent-created tools/code (developer code memories), planner sub-plans/sub-intentions, and human-crafted tool demonstrations / few-shot style demonstrations (semantic memory).
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID: semantic memory is a (relatively static) externally-provided store of human-crafted tools and transfer-learning demonstrations, while episodic memory is a GROWING store the agents write online from their own successful executions; retrieval queries both stores with the same similarity scoring.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval. The system retrieves a fixed number of items per store (semantic limit 3; episodic limit 4 for planner, 6 for developer); no explicit completeness/minimal-set objective is formulated.
retrieval_unit: For the developer: code memories (tool creation episodes / executable code blocks summarized before embedding). For the planner: sub-plan / sub-intention decompositions (planning trajectory chunks segmented via markdown headers). More broadly each episodic unit is a full task-solving trajectory e={task, (s0,a0)...(s_done,a_done)}; semantic memory units are human-crafted tool examples and style demonstrations.
index_source: Hybrid construction: semantic memory is offline/human-induced (manually crafted tools + curated WebShaper transfer samples for cold-start); episodic memory is online/test-time-induced, grown from the agent's own successful task executions during curriculum progression.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense+sparse vector indices, maintained as agent-specific repositories (one per sub-agent: planner repository and developer repository). Within episodic memory, t-SNE analysis shows emergent thematic clusters (e.g., search/fetch utilities, file I/O, browser automation, multimodal) but clustering is observed/analytical, not an explicit indexing topology.
retriever_type: Hybrid dense-sparse retrieval: dense embeddings via text-embedding-3-large plus sparse representations via Splade_PP_en_v2, combined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf). Retrieval uses pretrained embedding models (text-embedding-3-large, Splade_PP_en_v2) with RRF fusion; the retriever itself is not trained or RL-optimized. The only 'learning signal' on the retrievable store is which trajectories succeed (success-gated write-back), not retriever parameter training.
query_construction: The query is formed by the abstraction function Phi applied to the current task and state: Phi({tau, (s_t, .)}). Action-space-specific: code-writing actions are summarized (to reduce implementation noise) before embedding; planning agents perform intention decomposition and augmentation on proposed plans before embedding. Effectively an intent/summary-conditioned query.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/state-level: retrieval is conditioned on current task tau and current state s_t (Eq. 5-6, 8), and it is performed within the planner loop and the developer inner loop, so queries are constructed at the sub-plan / code-generation step level rather than only once at t=0.
when_to_retrieve: iterative: retrieval is interleaved with execution: the planner retrieves at sub-plan steps and the developer retrieves within its iterative code-generation/debugging inner loop, each conditioned on the evolving state s_t.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule tied to the workflow loop structure (no learned router or uncertainty trigger described): retrieval is invoked at each planner sub-plan step and at each developer code-generation step. [uncertain] whether retrieval fires on every single inner-loop iteration or once per developer task assignment.
reranking: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) over dense and sparse retrieval result lists to select the final top-k candidates. No cross-encoder or hierarchy-aware reranker is used.
retrieved_context_refinement: Pre-storage processing (abstraction/summarization of code memories and intention decomposition/augmentation of plans) plus RRF fusion; at use time, retrieved fragments are concatenated into the prompt. Markdown-header segmentation keeps chunks manageable; no explicit distractor-filtering or reason-in-documents distillation stage at retrieval time.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation + skill/tool reuse: retrieved memories m_t are concatenated with task and state (tau (+) s_t (+) m_t) and conditioned on procedural memory, so the policy samples actions a_t ~ pi(tau (+) s_t (+) m_t | M_proc). Concretely, retrieved code memories provide reusable tool implementations for the developer and retrieved sub-plans guide the planner.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved within a nested two-loop workflow: an outer planner loop performs task decomposition / sub-intent generation, and an inner developer-tester loop performs iterative code generation and debugging in a sandbox; retrieval feeds both loops. Retrieve-then-act at each step (planner retrieves plans, developer retrieves code). Augmented with 3-path sampling and LLM-as-a-judge consensus over the full rollout.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-tool-call / per-step within a rollout: retrieval and tool (code) creation occur per sub-plan (planner) and per code-generation step (developer inner loop), rather than per-token or only per final answer.
retrieved_item_representation: Surface form injected: for the developer, summarized executable code / tool snippets (program-or-skill); for the planner, free-text sub-plan/intention decompositions; plus human-crafted tool examples and style demonstrations from semantic memory. So a mix of executable-program and free-text-workflow representations.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mixed: reusable procedural skill (developer-created tools / code), reusable workflow (planner sub-plan decompositions), and single demonstration (human-crafted tool examples in semantic memory). Code is abstracted via summarization rather than stored as raw trajectory.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Primarily relevance/consensus-based: 3-path multi-path sampling with an independent reasoning LLM-as-a-judge (o4-mini) consensus critic filters incorrect trajectories before answers/experiences are accepted; code summarization reduces implementation noise; a 5-step lookback window during trajectory summarization avoids biased critic evaluation. Only successful (critic-validated) experiences are written, implicitly filtering noisy memory. No retriever-aware/distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: Hierarchical cognitive memory: procedural (system prompts + LLM parameters), semantic (human-crafted tools / transfer demonstrations), and episodic (online task-execution experiences = agent-created tools and sub-plans). Episodic + skill-library + procedural combined.
write_back: Yes. Upon successful task completion the complete execution trajectory is summarized/embedded via Phi and appended to the agent's episodic memory repository (M_ep <- M_ep U {e}); created tools likewise accumulate (T <- T U {T}).
online_growth: Yes. The episodic store grows during deployment/curriculum execution; the paper explicitly shows memory utilization shifting from semantic (human tools) toward episodic (agent-created tools/subplans) as the curriculum progresses (near-zero to saturation).
write_back_trigger: on-success only: experiences are written upon successful task completion (critic/consensus-validated success); failed trajectories are not stored (the paper notes leveraging failures as negative samples only as future work).
failure_experience_usage: success-only in the current system. Failed/negative experiences are NOT stored or retrieved; the authors explicitly list 'enhanced error utilization' treating failures as negative samples and verifier-based error attribution as future work (Sec. 6).
memory_evolution_update: append-only: successful trajectories/tools are added to the repository; no dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or forget-prune mechanism is described. (The paper notes a concern that self-generated tools increasingly displace human demonstrations in retrieval, but this is emergent retrieval preference, not an explicit mutation/forgetting policy.)
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Case/experience selection is fixed similarity-based top-k (dense+sparse with RRF) over off-the-shelf embeddings; it is not an RL-optimized or learned retrieval policy. (Contrast: Memento's M-MDP soft Q-learning is cited as related, but SMITH does not use a learned retrieval policy.)
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Cross-task and cross-agent within one workflow: each sub-agent (planner, developer) keeps its own agent-specific episodic repository, and experiences are shared across tasks (cross-task experience sharing is the core claim). Sharing is across roles/agents inside the SMITH workflow rather than across heterogeneous external agent frameworks.
benchmarks: GAIA benchmark (165 validation tasks with human-annotated difficulty Levels 1/2/3; 300 i.i.d. test samples mentioned for final evaluation). WebShaper dataset used as curated cold-start/transfer source for semantic memory (not as an evaluation benchmark).
benchmark_family: general AI assistant / agentic tool-use benchmark (GAIA) — spans QA, multi-hop reasoning, web search, file/multimodal handling, and tool-use.
baselines: Tool creation: Alita (75.2%). Experience sharing: Memento (70.9%). Multi-agent w. tool+memory: WebShaper-32B (53.3%), AutoAgent (55.2%), OpenDeepResearch (55.2%), TapeAgents (55.8%), OWL (69.7%), Manus (73.9%), MiroFlow (74.5%), AWorld (77.6%). Python-interpreter w/o tool reuse: SmolAgents (49.7%), OAgents (66.7%). Also internal base-model baselines: claude-4-sonnet (78.8%), claude-3.7-sonnet (70.9%), gpt-4.1 (67.9%).
key_metrics: Pass@1 (primary) and Pass@3 accuracy on GAIA, broken down by difficulty Level 1/2/3.
headline_result: 81.8% Pass@1 on the GAIA validation set (new SOTA), vs Alita 75.2% (+6.6) and Memento 70.9% (+10.9); Level 1 94.3%, Level 2 80.2%, Level 3 61.5%.
ablations: Component-removal ablations (Table 3 / Fig. 3): removing curriculum learning -10.3% (81.8 -> 71.5); removing episodic memory sharing -13.9% (-> 67.9); removing cold-start demonstration -21.8% (-> 60.0). Multi-path/self-critic ablation (Table 2): self-critic ensemble 81.8% vs best single model claude-4-sonnet 78.8% (+3.0), with consistent gains across levels (+1.8 L1, +3.5 L2, +3.8 L3). Curriculum re-estimation transforms the 3-level GAIA distribution into a balanced 4-level (L'=4) linearly-declining distribution.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (Pass@1/Pass@3 by level) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately. Memory behavior is analyzed qualitatively (memory-utilization trend, t-SNE clustering, 165x165 cross-task sharing correlation matrix) but not as quantitative retrieval scores.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Predominantly outcome-only (final-answer Pass@1/Pass@3). Process is examined qualitatively: memory-utilization evolution across curriculum, episodic-memory t-SNE clustering, cross-task experience-sharing correlation matrix, and failure-case analysis (OCR, Google Maps, repetitive scripting, oversized PDFs) — but not via quantitative step-wise/process metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Limited quantitative reporting. Uses 3-path sampling (cites AWorld: ~10% gain for 3-path, ~20% for 10-path on GAIA) trading more rollouts/compute for accuracy. Cold-start tool injection is motivated as reducing early trial-and-error / exploration variance. No explicit API-cost, latency, or token-savings numbers are reported. [uncertain] on concrete cost figures.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k selection: semantic memory search limit = 3; episodic memory limit = 4 for the planner and 6 for the developer (m=4 planner, n=6 developer fragments). RRF selects the final top-k candidates. No adaptive-k or explicit token budget is reported.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing GAIA: 165 validation tasks, 3 human-annotated difficulty levels, 300 i.i.d. test samples; SMITH re-estimates difficulty into L'=4 levels but does not construct a new benchmark).
cbr_cycle_coverage: Implicitly Retrieve + Reuse (and Retain via success-gated write-back); Revise is partial via the developer-tester debug-and-refine loop on freshly generated code rather than adaptation of a retrieved case. Approx: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: partial, Retain: yes].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself via cognitive architectures for language agents (Sumers et al. 2023) and episodic/semantic/procedural memory, not as case-based reasoning; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner.
tool_document_engineering: Human-crafted tools follow a standardized structure: a clear title/function description, a descriptive usage-scenario paragraph, and a minimalist commented Python implementation (Fig. 12 style demonstration). Agent-created code memories undergo LLM summarization before embedding to reduce implementation noise. No synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned tool embeddings.
index_content_separation: Partial: code memories are summarized into lightweight descriptions for indexing while the underlying implementation is the heavier content; the developer retrieves based on function description and recalls concise task-specific snippets (avoiding lengthy irrelevant code). Not a formal progressive-disclosure/index-then-content protocol.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Dynamic/live-growing tool store: the tool repository evolves online (T <- T U {T}). SMITH autonomously installs Python packages (e.g., pdfplumber, serpapi, scholarly, whisper, faster_whisper) at runtime and autonomously leverages Model Context Protocol (MCP) via fastmcp without pre-configured semantic memory. Tools are created as Python code in a sandbox (function-calling / code-execution) rather than via a fixed RapidAPI/RESTful registry; no formal CRUD auto-sync protocol.
tool_dependency_awareness: Not explicitly modeled. Retrieval is similarity-based over individual code/tool memories; no inter-tool dependency graph, shared-auth modeling, or dependency-aware reranking is described. Tool composition is left to the agent's iterative code generation.
adaptation_mechanism: execution-feedback-driven revision (for freshly generated code) plus verbatim/LLM-prompted reuse of retrieved code and plans: retrieved memories are injected as in-context guidance; the developer-tester inner loop revises code via sandbox error feedback until success. Not RL-reuse-finetuning and not critic-only adaptation of a retrieved case.
builds_on: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (Sumers et al. 2023, episodic/semantic/procedural memory); retrieval-augmented generation (Lewis et al. 2020); tool creation lines Alita, CRAFT, CREATOR, LATM, ToolMaker, SmolAgents (save/cache generated tools); experience-sharing/memory lines Memento (M-MDP), MAEL, CoPS, Mem0, MemGPT, Generative Agents, ReAct; workflow-agent designs OWL and OAgents; multi-path sampling + LLM-as-a-judge from AWorld and SciMaster; WebShaper used for cold-start transfer.
contrasts_with: Alita (tool creation from scratch without systematic experience reuse), Memento (cross-task experience sharing without integrated tool creation), Toolformer/predefined-tool learning (limited coverage), and parameter-based experience methods (AWorld, WebShaper SFT+RL) that lack clear memory hierarchies and continual inference-time learning. SMITH's claimed novelty is unifying tool creation + experience sharing in one cognitive memory architecture.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): tool-creation + cross-task experience sharing line. Sits at the intersection of dynamic tool creation (Alita / CRAFT / CREATOR / LATM / SmolAgents) and episodic experience-sharing memory agents (Memento / MAEL / CoPS), unified under a cognitive (procedural/semantic/episodic) memory architecture for general AI assistants on GAIA.
